sources.role: Not an OpenMS header. BSpline2d is a PIMPL wrapper around this vendored library, so the library is the real implementation this port had to reproduce.
Domain, boundary-condition and basis declarations; documents the Ooyama formulation and the node-count heuristic.
solve/evaluate/slope; the mean-subtraction and the evaluation window are ported from here.
Setup, Alpha, Beta, Basis, DBasis, qDelta, calculateQ, addP. Holds the truncated PI, the float accumulators and the out-of-range Beta reads.
Explicit template instantiation for float and double; fixes T = double for OpenMS.
Banded storage plus LU_factor_banded and LU_solve_banded; the out-of-band scratch element and the pre-update zero-pivot check come from here.

fixtures.role: The BSpline2d class test's data: x = seq(-5,5,0.1) plus Gaussian noise, y = 10*sin(x) plus noise, resampled with replacement and re-ordered by x, so abscissae repeat. Used for the 202-point fit whose 405 coefficients are compared one by one.

stdout of ../oracle/msc_splines/probe_strict, one `case<TAB>key<TAB>value` row per observation at %.17g. Covers 12 CubicSpline2d positions with all three derivative orders, the class test's sine grid, seven error paths, 13 BSpline2d configurations with every node coefficient, the class test's mean-squared-error assertions, 27 BSplineSmoothingSpline fits and 10 spline_bisection brackets.

Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0
Thread model: posix
adaptations: OpenMS/config.h, OpenMS/OpenMSConfig.h, CONCEPT/Types.h, CONCEPT/Macros.h, CONCEPT/Exception.h and CONCEPT/LogStream.h are shims: an empty OPENMS_DLLAPI, Size/UInt typedefs, an inert OPENMS_PRECONDITION as in a release build, a std::runtime_error-derived Exception::IllegalArgument, and an OPENMS_LOG_ERROR that writes to a discarded ostringstream so stdout stays machine readable.
No MATH/MISC translation unit and no eol-bspline file is modified; BSplineLib.cpp instantiates the templates exactly as the OpenMS build does.

The driver additionally constructs eol_bspline::BSpline<double> alongside each OpenMS BSpline2d so the node count, node domain, penalty weight and basis coefficients that the PIMPL wrapper hides are observable.

determinism.note: A second build at -O0 with the same -ffp-contract=off produced byte-identical output (sha256 5be8b1aeccbbbd150a918bf44055074883578981a9b6e3cca5de7682e47b06e9).

floating_point_contraction.note: The same sources built without -ffp-contract=off, which is clang's default, differ from the strict output in 2 638 of the printed digits' last one or two units in the last place, because clang fuses multiply-adds into FMA on arm64. The strict build is the recorded oracle because it is what a compiler without FMA contraction produces and is therefore reproducible on any target; the difference is a portability property of the C++ and is documented in docs/BSPLINE2D_SUPPORT.md.

class_test_review.note: Every START_SECTION of the four class tests is reproduced by a named Rust test; docs/*_SUPPORT.md name the test and one concrete asserted value per section.

source_anchors.operation: adjacent_find with std::greater accepts equal neighbouring abscissae, which then divide by a zero interval width in init_
eval steps back one knot when lower_bound overshoots or when x is the last knot, so the last segment is evaluated at its right end
c_.back() = 0 and the recurrence leaving c_[0] = 0 are the natural boundary condition
PI is the truncated literal 3.1415927, which feeds Alpha
Setup rewrites a zero cutoff wavelength to 1.0, so the derivative constraint is never actually disabled
the node search starts at ten intervals, so an automatic node count with a positive wavelength needs at least eleven points
calculateQ holds b1, b2 and the accumulator in float, rounding the boundary correction to single precision
the lower-right boundary loop calls Beta(M-4), which reads BoundaryConditions[bc][-1] when M < 4; the result is written to a banded coordinate that discards it
addP holds every basis value and every product in a float before accumulating into the double normal matrix
the ordinate mean is subtracted before the fit and added back in evaluate, which is why evaluation far outside the domain returns the mean
evaluate sums only the four basis functions around the query node and clamps the window to [0, M], so the sum is empty beyond two node intervals
LU_factor_banded tests the pre-update diagonal for zero, then divides by the post-update one
LU_solve_banded divides by A(M, M) without the zero check the rest of the loop performs
a polynomial fit is accepted when its residual sum of squares is within ten percent of the budget, which is why a coarse fit can beat an exact one
the candidate comparator is not a strict weak ordering; with at most six candidates libstdc++ runs insertion sort, so the result is the stable one
lefthand_sign is seeded true and never updated, reducing the exclusive-or to the sign of the midpoint derivative
the do/while has no iteration cap and does not terminate when the midpoint stops moving

native_boundaries: CubicSpline2d requires strictly increasing finite abscissae; the source accepts non-decreasing ones and then produces NaN coefficients.
BSpline2d and BSplineSmoothingSpline return Err where the source leaves an object whose ok() is false; BSpline2d::ok stays for the post-construction solve failure the source can still reach.
BSpline2d caps input at 250 000 points and 500 001 nodes, so the banded matrix never exceeds 28 MiB; the source bounds neither.
spline_bisection caps the loop at 4 096 halvings and requires a finite positive threshold; the source can loop forever.
Every evaluation and every recurrence intermediate is checked for finiteness, so a non-finite result is an error rather than a silently propagated NaN.
calculateQ skips the (i, j) pairs the C++ computes from an out-of-range Beta and then discards; the discarded-write argument is in docs/BSPLINE2D_SUPPORT.md and the result is numerically identical.
No OpenMP: the source carries no pragma in these four files, so there is no parallelism gap to record.
external_reference_note: The probe driver and its shim headers live outside this repository under ../oracle/msc_splines/ so that no C++ is committed here. The unmodified scientific translation units and the vendored eol-bspline files are copied there from the pinned checkout at build time; their sha256 values are the ones listed under `sources`, so the chain from the pinned revision to the committed probe output is complete. They are recorded, not re-verified by the in-repo gate, because they are intentionally absent from the crate.
